page: Amazon Web Services c7g.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance utilizing the 64-bit ARM architecture. The server is equipped with 64 dedicated physical cores based on the AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 design, running at a nominal clock frequency of 2.6 GHz with one execution thread per core. Memory configuration includes 128 GB of DDR5 RAM, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2 GB per core. The server includes no onboard local NVMe storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, relying on remote network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 30 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate pronounced capabilities in parallel computation and memory-intensive throughput. Multi-core performance is highlighted by Geekbench scores and Clang compilation metrics that place within the top tier of evaluated hardware. The memory subsystem benefits from DDR5 bandwidth, delivering 276.84 GB/s in large-block read operations and a top-decile PassMark memory score. Single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core results, place in the middle 50 percent, while sequential language model token generation exhibits low performance.

Direct physical hardware access removes hypervisor virtualization penalties and eliminates noisy-neighbor variability. Qualitative cost efficiency is supported by high core density and power-efficient ARM architecture, maximizing execution throughput per server footprint compared to traditional architectures. Primary tradeoffs include the lack of local temporary storage and baseline single-core performance. The server fits high-concurrency software build systems, parallel continuous integration pipelines, static web serving clusters, and in-memory key-value databases like Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.metal is a compute-optimized bare-metal server powered by 64 dedicated 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 cores clocked at 2.6 GHz with single-threaded core execution. The configuration is equipped with 128 GB of DDR5 memory, allocating 2 GB per core, and delivers a baseline network throughput of 30 Gbps. It contains no onboard local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, depending entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-threaded processing and memory subsystem bandwidth, with Geekbench multi-core scores and Clang compilation metrics ranking in the upper decile, alongside high Redis transaction rates. Conversely, single-threaded execution and sequential LLM token generation remain average. The bare-metal design eliminates hypervisor contention, offering high resource density and qualitative cost advantages for parallel ARM-native computing. The instance is suited for large-scale software compilation, continuous integration pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, and distributed caching infrastructures.
